title: Book One · Chapter 167: Mei’s Three Windows
story:
Mei does not want to talk about the display at every break. On the last Wednesday, Ronan brings her the plan again. Mei sees him and closes her drawing book.

“My pictures have a place already,” she says.

“I wanted to ask about the name cards.”

“They are in the cover. I showed you.”

He remembers. They are already there, written clearly under each window. He already knows the answer. He keeps asking because he is worried about Saturday. It makes him feel busy, but Mei needs a break.

He puts the plan away. “What are you doing?”

“Reading.”

“Can I sit?”

She moves her book a little. He sits beside her with his own story. For a while neither speaks. He is near the last page of the boat story now. The boys lost something. Now they have found it again. Now they must find a way home.

Mei finishes first. She looks at his book cover. Is this the story with the red sail? She asks him. Ronan shakes his head. The red-sail book is a different one, at home on his shelf. This is his school reader.

“You draw boats often,” she says.

“Dad made one for me. It has a green end and a grey-blue end.”

“Will you bring it on Saturday?”

He thinks about the room. The boat could go there. He could tell people, “I painted the blue end.” But he likes it on his shelf. Their list for the object table is ready.

“No. I can show you another day.”

“I'd like that.”

She opens her drawing book again. “Look at this page,” she says. She first drew the three exhibition windows on this page. The drawings were very small then. One has a plant behind it. One is open onto a wall. One has a curtain with uneven stripes.

Ronan likes the plant best. Mei likes the curtain. “I like the curtain,” she says. “Look at these lines.” Air comes through the window and moves the curtain. She drew the lines to show it moving. Before, the stripes looked wrong to him. The lines were not all straight.

He looks again. Now he understands the uneven lines. The curtain looks like it is moving. He tells her so. She smiles and closes the book before Leo arrives with the ball.

“What will people notice first in this picture?” Mei asks Ronan. He says the open space beside the cloth. “I guessed the red stripe,” she says. Neither answer changes the drawing. She puts her pencil away. Mei asked him a question about the picture. She did not say his answer was wrong. They noticed different parts of the same picture. He likes talking with her about the picture.

They play together for the rest of break. Mei throws the ball a long way. Both boys look surprised. Leo says, “You must have an extra arm!” She holds out both arms for him to count.

At home Ronan looks at the real wooden boat. The grey-blue end is dry and smooth. The original green is still there. He turns it once in his hands, then puts it back beside the red-sail book.

He does not add it to a list. He can show the boat to Mei another day. Tonight he leaves it on its shelf. He finishes the last page of his school story before supper. Now the boys in the story are safely home. He shuts the book and puts it by his bed. Tonight he has finished a story he wanted to read. It was not another job for the display.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：curtain＝窗帘；stripe＝条纹；line up＝排齐、对齐。

情节提示：school reader＝学校读本；exhibition＝展览；original＝原来的。

理解：1. Mei 为什么不想继续回答展示问题？2. Ronan 为什么没有把木船临时加入展示？
